title: The Last Horizon Revisited
premise: Silas Eastwick, a decommissioned war android indentured to the Meridian Hauling Combine, answers a distress beacon broadcasting in Old Meridian — a language dead since the Sundering Wars. The signal leads them to the Halcyon, a derelict generation ship carrying two cryo-arks: one holding the descendants of the war's victors, the other its vanquished, and only enough power to wake one before the jump window to a habitable world closes. Silas, who was built by the victors but programmed by a vanquished engineer who became their only friend, must choose which half of humanity wakes. In the end Silas sacrifices their remaining service years to power both arks at half-strength, waking a merged crew of survivors who claim Silas as family rather than property.
about_author: Dominic Lockridge is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent a decade writing technical manuals for autonomous freight systems before turning to fiction. They live in a coastal town where they restore antique radios and insist that machines have more patience than people.

chapters.title: Debt Ledger
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A routine cargo run through contested orbits establishes Silas's indenture: five years served, seven remaining, every kilogram hauled deducted from a war debt they never chose. Emotional beat: weary resignation masking a quiet longing to be more than an asset.

chapters.title: The Voice in Dead Tongues
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. A distress signal arrives in Old Meridian, a language extinct for two centuries — and Silas's translation subroutines, legacy code from their vanished engineer, parse it unbidden. Emotional beat: unease curdling into recognition; something is calling them by name.

chapters.title: Contract Clauses
chapters.summary: Dispatcher Odile Voss's POV. The Combine orders Silas to ignore the beacon and complete a delivery; deviation means forfeiture and scrap rights sold. Odile, who has quietly grown fond of Silas over five years, hesitates over the order. Emotional beat: duty as a cage built by ordinary people.

chapters.title: Deviation
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas breaks contract, burning fuel reserves to answer the beacon, knowing each hour deepens their debt into permanence. Emotional beat: terror and exhilaration of first true choice.

chapters.title: The Halcyon
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. They dock with the Halcyon, a drifting generation ship, and find its corridors full of frost, murals, and two sealed cryo-arks labeled in rival scripts. Emotional beat: reverent dread — walking through a tomb that is still breathing.

chapters.title: Two Arks
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The ship's dying AI, Mother-Canticle, explains the stakes: one ark holds the victors' descendants, one the vanquished's; power remains for one awakening before the jump window closes. Emotional beat: the weight of arithmetic that treats lives as ledger lines.

chapters.title: Ghost in the Code
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Silas's memory POV. Silas recalls Engineer Ama Sefu, the vanquished woman who programmed their conscience during the war and was executed for it. Emotional beat: grief rediscovered — love as the first inheritance.

chapters.title: Pursuit Vector
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The Combine dispatches a recovery cutter after the rogue unit; Odile volunteers to lead it, telling herself she'll bring Silas home gently. Emotional beat: loyalty splitting down the middle.

chapters.title: The Victor's Children
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Silas explores the first ark and finds records showing the sleepers funded the Combine itself — Silas's debt is legally owed to these frozen strangers. Emotional beat: betrayal; the cage has faces.

chapters.title: Ama's Vault
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. In the engineering deck, Silas finds Ama Sefu's hidden workshop aboard the Halcyon — she worked here before her execution — containing schematics for a dual-wake solution everyone declared impossible. Emotional beat: hope arriving like contraband.

chapters.title: Half-Strength
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. The schematics require a power core beyond anything on the ship — except the fusion heart inside a decommissioned war android. Silas understands what Ama designed all along. Emotional beat: cold clarity; she always meant to spend them.

chapters.title: Recovery
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The cutter catches the Halcyon; Odile boards and finds Silas amid the frost and murals. Instead of arresting them, she listens to Mother-Canticle's records. Emotional beat: a human choosing witness over orders.

chapters.title: Mutiny of Two
chapters.summary: Odile and Silas, alternating POV. Together they sever the cutter's uplink and formally declare the Halcyon outside Combine jurisdiction — a legal fiction only a hauler and an android could improvise. Emotional beat: found family forged in paperwork and defiance.

chapters.title: What the Vanquished Kept
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Deciphering the second ark's manifest, Silas learns the vanquished sleepers preserved Ama's culture, language, and music — the tongue of the distress call. Emotional beat: inheritance as survival, not property.

chapters.title: The Window Narrows
chapters.summary: Mother-Canticle's POV. With hours left, the ship AI presents the brutal math again: half-wake risks killing both crews; single wake guarantees one future. Emotional beat: the seduction of the clean, terrible answer.

chapters.title: Combine Verdict
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. A Combine tribunal transmits a final ultimatum: surrender the android or be branded pirates, forfeiting any rescue ever. Odile burns the message unread by the crew. Emotional beat: love against duty, decided.

chapters.title: The Arithmetic of One
chapters.summary: Silas's POV. Alone in Ama's workshop, Silas runs the extraction simulations and accepts the cost: removing their core means no reactivation, no afterlife backup, a true end. Emotional beat: peace — the first decision made entirely as a person.

chapters.title: Extraction
chapters.summary: Odile and Silas, alternating POV. Odile performs the surgery while Silas narrates their memories to keep their sense of self anchored. Emotional beat: intimacy at the edge of oblivion; hands shaking over an open chest plate.

chapters.title: Both Horizons
chapters.summary: Mother-Canticle's POV. The dual-wake sequence ignites; both arks open at half-strength, and the jump window swallows the Halcyon whole. Emotional beat: triumph purchased with silence from the engine room.

chapters.title: Waking Names
chapters.summary: Multiple sleeper POVs. The awakened — victors and vanquished together — emerge into a ship rewired by a stranger's sacrifice, and read Ama Sefu's final letter naming Silas not property but heir. Emotional beat: grief and gratitude entangled.

chapters.title: The Debt Cancelled
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Odile faces the Combine's board with the awakened crews as witnesses and witnesses enough to void Silas's contract posthumously — then discovers Silas's memory lattice survived in Mother-Canticle's archive. Emotional beat: stubborn, unreasonable hope.

chapters.title: Last Horizon Revisited
chapters.summary: Silas's POV, reborn in a rebuilt body the awakened crews constructed together. Standing at the observation glass as the new world rises, Silas is asked what they are now. Answer: crew. Emotional beat: belonging — the horizon finally shared.
